Exercise 2: Design the Data Cloud-triggered flow

html:
Data 360 turns the CRM from a source of records into a consumer of a unified profile. Sales and Service implementations surface Data 360 data inside Lightning without duplicating it, respond with Data Cloud-triggered flows, and grow richer as agents and copilots gain profile context. This phase covers the CRM side: related lists, enrichment, flows, and the service-cloud patterns that this lab's UnifiedProfileEnrichmentService and CaseTriggerHandlerService demonstrate.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Enable and explain Data 360 data in Lightning (profile data, Data Cloud-triggered flows, related lists).
  • Configure a Data Cloud-triggered flow to personalize a Case/Lead/Account record.
  • Explain enrichment vs write-back and when each is appropriate.
  • Read this lab's UnifiedProfileEnrichmentService + Case trigger wiring as a CRM-side mirror.

1. Data 360 in the CRM: the "consume" side

Data 360 licences include the CRM integrations that put unified data next to reps and agents:

Consumption featureWhat it doesConfiguration
Data Cloud-triggered flowsA Flow with a Data 360 data source/start that runs when Data 360 records changeSetup → Data 360 → Data Cloud-triggered flows
Related lists / Data 360 dataShow unified-profile attributes or related Data 360 records on the record pageLightning App Builder → Data 360 components
Data actionsCRM (or external) side effects triggered by Data 360 eventsData actions + flows (Phase 10)
EnrichmentCopy Data 360 attributes onto CRM records (materialised)Data action / flow write-back
Agentforce / Copilot groundingUnified profile in agent promptsData Graphs / retrievers (Phase 14)

Enrichment vs on-the-fly

  • On-the-fly display keeps the CRM clean: the record page reads the Data 360 profile without duplicating data into Contact/Case.
  • Materialized enrichment writes Data 360 attributes (e.g. Lifetime_Value__c, Last_Case_Sentiment__c) onto CRM fields for reporting, search, and offline/Salesforce1 consumption.
  • Trade-off: enrichment is denormalized and must be kept fresh; on-the-fly is always current but is a view, not queryable CRM data. The exam asks you to choose per requirement (reporting need = materialize; live context need = on-the-fly/view).

2. Data Cloud-triggered flows (service scenario)

A Data Cloud-triggered flow runs when Data 360 records change. Typical service flow:

  1. Start: "receive a Data Change Event" on the UnifiedIndividual/Case DMO when a segment member qualifies or a profile attribute changes (e.g. churn score updates).
  2. Lookup CRM: find the Contact/Case by sfdc_recordId or the external key.
  3. Branch: if churn score high → update Case (set Priority), else → no-op.
  4. Act: update/create records, fire a data action, or notify an agent.

Because Data 360 events can be high-volume, flows must be selective (filter in the start/decision), idempotent, and read data via the flow's Data 360 data source component. The lab mirrors the "contract" with Apex on the CRM side (below) so the pattern is testable without provisioning a Data 360 org.

3. The Service example carried through this lab

When a Case is created or updated, CaseTriggerHandlerService calls UnifiedProfileEnrichmentService to simulate pulling the unified profile's key attributes (lifetime spend, churn risk, consent-permitted channels) onto the case. This is the same design a Data Cloud-triggered flow performs declaratively:

apex
public with sharing class UnifiedProfileEnrichmentService {
    public static void enrichCases(List<Case> cases) {
        // 1. Collect the customer keys we care about
        // 2. "Fetch" the unified-profile summary for those keys (lab: Consent_Preference__c + KPI_Metric__c lookups)
        // 3. Enrich in memory, no DML here (before-update context)
    }
}

Lesson: enrichment logic reads once, applies to a bulk batch, mutates in memory (before-save), and never loops DML. Exactly the discipline the exam grades.

Related lists & "just the profile"

For a pure display requirement, the config answer is a Data 360-related-list/component showing the unified profile (or Data 360 records like recent orders) — no field copies, no ETL. Remember this classic answer pairing:

RequirementCorrect answer
"Agent wants live spend + churn on the case page"Data 360 component/related list (on-the-fly)
"Salesforce1/reporting needs spend as a filterable field"Materialise via data action/flow enrichment
"Playbooks route based on churn bucket"Materialise then use in flow/assignment rules

4. Sales specifics (quick map)

  • Lead enrichment: score/route leads using Data 360 attributes (e.g. firmographic Headcount, Spend) at conversion; the data-action layer fetches unified-account data.
  • Opportunity context: related-list of a customer's Data 360 orders/engagements so sellers see activity beyond the single opp.
  • Clean data in = good model out: ingestion quality on Account/Contact mapping directly affects sales routing quality.

Service specifics are where this repo lives: case enrichment, escalation context, and consent-aware messaging (Phase 11).

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: On-the-fly vs materialize

For each: (a) agent console wants live order history; (b) a report filters cases by customer tenure; (c) an omni-script uses churn tier. Pick on-the-fly vs materialize and justify.

Exercise 2: Design the Data Cloud-triggered flow

Write the flow pseudo-steps for "churn ≥ 0.7 triggers Priority=High + notify CSM on the Case": start event, filter, lookup, branch, update, notify. Note where you would use a Data Change Event vs a segment qualification event.

Exercise 3: Enrich in the lab

Open UnifiedProfileEnrichmentServiceTest. Add a case set where two customers have known lifetime spend and verify enrichment writes Lifetime_Value__c/churn fields for exactly those customers and leaves unknown customers untouched.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Data Cloud-triggered flowFlow started by a Data 360 data change/qualification event, acting on CRM records.
Related list (Data 360 data)Lightning component showing unified-profile/Data 360 records on a record page.
EnrichmentCopying Data 360 attributes onto CRM records (materialised).
On-the-fly displayShowing Data 360 data live without duplicating into CRM fields.
Write-back / data actionA side effect (CRM update, external call) triggered by a Data 360 event.
sfdc_recordIdThe CRM record id carried on the DMO to link back.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can choose on-the-fly vs materialized enrichment for a requirement.
  • I can design a Data Cloud-triggered flow end-to-end (event → filter → lookup → act).
  • I can explain where Data 360 data appears in the Service/Sales Console.
  • I can read and test UnifiedProfileEnrichmentService.

Self-Check

  1. Q: "Agents want to SEE live purchase history on the case page." — A: Data 360-related-list/component on the record page (on-the-fly; no field copies).
  2. Q: "IT wants cases filterable by customer lifetime value in a report." — A: Materialise Lifetime_Value__c onto Case/Account via enrichment/data action, then report.
  3. Q: Why does enrichment mutate in memory instead of DML-looping in the trigger? — A: Before-save context + bulk discipline: one batch, one saved transaction, no per-record DML.
